flags.note: The שֶׁל genitive construction is frequent throughout this text. While not impossible in late Hebrew, the high frequency suggests Greek influence where genitive case would be used.

flags.hebrew: ואתה אינה יודע באיזה זמן שאבא
flags.note: The word order with אינה יודע mirrors Greek οὐ γινώσκεις. Native Hebrew would more naturally use לא תדע or אינך יודע.
Multiple שֶׁל genitives continue the pattern suggesting Greek genitive influence.
The construction ואינה כופר follows Greek syntax. Native Hebrew would use ולא כפרת or similar with proper subject-verb agreement.
Another שֶׁל-type genitive construction (implied), though here using מ- prefix, still reflecting Greek genitive patterns.
The construction with שהמה + future verb follows Greek ἵνα + subjunctive pattern rather than natural Hebrew subordination.
Continues the pattern of שֶׁל genitive constructions influenced by Greek genitive case.
Complex genitive relationships that mirror Greek case syntax rather than natural Hebrew construct chains.
The word order with the verb ירק placed before the subject אני mirrors Greek verb-subject order, unnatural in Hebrew.
The use of אינה (feminine form) with masculine subject follows Greek neuter participle constructions rather than Hebrew gender agreement.
The construction ובאם שאחד follows Greek conditional syntax (ἐάν τις) rather than natural Hebrew conditional patterns.
